links.scope: Dataset Preparation stopped before the next row when the test requested cancellation during either similarity pass. It wrote no dataset output.

limitations: The test used three made-up rows and did not run an app or model. Host and final qualification still need their own evidence.

links.scope: The same test used 2.98 MB of temporary Python memory instead of 9.27 MB. All rows and report values stayed the same. Median time went from 147 to 158 milliseconds.

links.scope: Add data stops reading the selected file when the app confirms cancellation. The form sends no more chunks and keeps the file selected.

links.scope: The managed browser reopened saved drafts and published assets after four server restarts. The test used a fresh local database and verified TLS.

links.scope: The managed browser reopened saved drafts and published assets after four server restarts. The test used a fresh local database and verified TLS.

links.scope: The real Desktop Publish renderer, client and preload opened and submitted a selected form with mocked IPC. Dedicated channels rejected mismatched responses.

links.scope: Managed record routes use the current active organization role and deny unavailable or mismatched authority.

links.scope: Packaged Desktop and the managed browser each passed four Form Composer cases on the same tested source, including published records and actual 400 percent editor and Preview reflow.
limitations: Uses test-owned local applications and synthetic records. The timing evidence is limited to this eight-page, 32-field fixture.

links.scope: A writer process stopped after SQLite committed. A new process recovered the same receipt and found one record and one linked audit entry, with no second committed action.

links.scope: The actual Canvas picker passed native 400 percent contrast, focus, and control fit on both local hosts.

limitations: The Properties evidence does not qualify the broader Canvas journey or other surfaces.

links.scope: The actual Canvas Preview passed native 400 percent normal and forced-color checks on both local hosts. Its accessible name still identifies the system.
limitations: The Preview evidence does not qualify the broader Canvas journey or other surfaces.

links.scope: The selected Layers row kept its matching system text color at actual 400 percent zoom on both local hosts. Normal and forced-color audits passed.

links.scope: Read-only source has its own theme foreground and background. Desktop Customizations passed the normal and forced-color audits at 400 percent zoom.

links.scope: The registered managed browser Canvas journey passed keyboard insertion, edit history, Preview, save and reopen. Picker, Properties, Preview and Layers passed at 1440 and 320 CSS pixels in normal and forced colors.

links.scope: The local Chromium Canvas case used Tab, Space, and Arrow Right to select all eight application layouts at 320 CSS pixels. Each choice kept keyboard focus after loading. The last layout survived save and reopen, and the element picker returned focus when closed.

links.scope: The packaged Windows app passed the Canvas application-layout keyboard journey at actual 400 percent zoom. The test selected all eight layouts, checked focus after each update, saved and reopened the last layout in the same workspace after a renderer reload, and verified that Escape in the element picker restored focus. The isolated app closed at the end.
limitations: This result covers application layouts on the packaged Windows app. See the separate page-layout result for both local hosts. The managed browser case remains unrun because its local database engine is unavailable.

links.scope: Local Chromium at 320 CSS pixels and the packaged Windows app at native 400 percent zoom both passed keyboard insertion of all six built-in page layouts. The test verified their layout category, vertical region order, lack of horizontal document overflow, and preserved Cards in the required regions after saving and reopening the revision.
limitations: The managed browser test is registered but has not run because its local database engine is unavailable. Production accessibility and the separate legacy review remain pending.

links.scope: Local Chromium passed keyboard switching between Canvas Design and Connections at 320 CSS pixels. Chromium and the packaged Windows app also passed at actual 400 percent zoom. The focused interaction test verified arrow keys, Home and End, selected tab and panel semantics, and preservation of unsaved edits when returning to Design.
limitations: This is a local test of tab navigation, focus and draft preservation. The full Connections workflow, managed browser, legacy security and broader production qualification remain pending.

links.scope: Local Chromium and the packaged Windows app passed a keyboard journey at actual 400 percent zoom. The tests added a typed connection between two preview assets, excluded an incompatible asset, validated and reopened the saved connection, removed it, and verified that it stayed removed after saving and reopening.
limitations: This result covers one typed connection between built-in preview assets on both local hosts. The managed browser test, broader accessibility and separate security review remain pending.

links.scope: The clean-checkout fixes let the standard Node runner start and allow the documentation gate to run without private files.
limitations: The combined test and dependency gates still require a passing current run.

links.scope: The Form recovery test passed in both source and compiled modes. A fresh process recovered the saved submission without creating a duplicate.
limitations: This result covers the isolated submission recovery test. It grants no new whole-roadmap qualification.

links.scope: Six Windows desktop Assets and Form Composer journeys passed. Both combined end-to-end groups also passed.
limitations: Browser contrast, managed restart, standard regression, development dependency and separate security evidence are still open.

links.scope: The browser test now uses the menu and Canvas controls available at narrow widths. It checks that the new workspace is selected before continuing.
limitations: The browser reached the Build and test dialog at 400 percent zoom. Its accessibility audit still needs a complete pass.

links.scope: The Build and test dialog now removes decorative motion when reduced motion is enabled. The browser passed the motion stage at 400 percent zoom.
limitations: The dialog contrast check is separate and remains open.

links.scope: The assistant response preview now exposes a named status without hiding its text. The focused preview and reference tests passed.
limitations: The contrast checks and overall browser qualification remain open.

links.scope: The combined packaged Windows run passed all four journeys. In 100 foreground revokes, 95 percent restored control within 6.3 ms. The slowest took 8 ms.
limitations: The tests used held replies to verify that an unresponsive window loses its lease. Timing under natural Windows background throttling and complete queue measurements are still pending.
In separate phases, the test held a display reply and a context reply. The native menu test then disabled takeover and confirmed that a separately paired editor could still save.

links.scope: Two PostgreSQL connections tried the same save. The database kept one saved result and returned that result on retry.
limitations: The test also confirmed rollback after permission was withdrawn before commit. Delivery to browsers connected to separate servers still needs a live test.

links.scope: The server can provide a small list of saved systems and changes to an authorized workspace member. Successful checks add no audit log entry.
limitations: The isolated tests confirmed workspace limits and access denial. An automated browser journey still needs to verify this behavior through the complete app.

links.scope: The server sends saved system changes over an authenticated connection. It closes the connection if access ends or it cannot keep up with sending updates.
limitations: A local HTTP test verified access loss and connection limits. Browser refresh, browser takeover and recovery across separate servers still need qualification.

links.scope: Browser refresh keeps an open Composer and its focus if another client archives the system. A delayed reply cannot update the view after the browser connection changes.
limitations: The browser feature tests passed. The complete journey with the built browser app, authenticated server and chat adapter is still pending.

links.scope: Focused tests confirmed that the server can tell the registered chat client and browser apart and reject a request with the wrong credentials.
limitations: This check covers client identity. The shared server routes and browser consent still need qualification.

links.scope: Two test servers sharing PostgreSQL delivered a saved change. After the test abruptly stopped one server, a replacement recovered both saved changes in about four seconds.
limitations: This was one local recovery test. Browser timing and production deployments remain outside this result.

links.scope: The official chat adapter saved a system on the running test server. Retrying returned the original result, and the browser credential saw one saved change.
limitations: This test did not interrupt the first reply. The full browser interaction and recovery from a lost reply still need tests.

links.scope: The server rejected a second valid credential for the same user when it tried to reuse the first tab’s proof. The test kept both credentials valid.
limitations: This test covers ownership on the server. The complete browser permission and revoke interaction still needs a live test.

links.scope: The built Chrome app opened the consent dialog without moving the Systems heading. The test accepted, revoked and reloaded the exact tab on the same server as the chat client.
limitations: Saved-resource presentation and performance still need separate tests.

links.scope: A focused browser UI test reached the consent dialog after retrying with the same credential when the test server reported it was full.
limitations: These checks cover tab consent recovery. They do not measure saved-state delivery.

links.scope: The server still checks access on every tab observation. The test confirmed that routine successful checks do not add audit records and consent actions keep their standard audit.
limitations: The audit tests cover the consent observation route.

links.scope: The managed chat client can request, check or release an eligible browser tab. Only the browser user can accept the request.
limitations: This review covers the four consent tools. Saved-resource delivery and live context remain pending.

links.scope: The server checks permission again before it sends saved item details to the tab that accepted control. The tab answers a short-lived request before chat can read its current view and saved item identifiers.
limitations: This review covers the server routes and access checks. The full browser and Windows comparison has separate requirements.

links.scope: The browser displays the chosen saved item after consent. Revoke closes it immediately. Focused tests confirm that late replies cannot display an item or share fresh context after revoke.
limitations: These tests cover the browser interface and delayed replies. They use simulated server responses.

links.scope: The reviewed Chrome test script checks that saved changes appear, the selected item displays in the resource panel, and the user can revoke control. Its optional timing mode collects 100 samples per action.
limitations: The linked review covers the test script. Hidden tabs and the final host comparison still need separate checks.

links.scope: The managed server refused the other Chrome tab’s attempt to accept the first tab’s control request. Revoking control left zero stale displays after the held reply was released. The first tab showed the latest save when it became visible again.
limitations: This test used the local managed server and PostgreSQL. The combined browser and Windows qualification is still open.

links.scope: A dialog that is already open pauses clicks and form submissions while control starts or is active. Revoke remains available and restores manual actions.
limitations: Focused interface tests cover this behavior.

links.scope: All 59 design requirements point to current test files and named checks. The record lists where a live browser or Windows test is still needed.
limitations: The links identify test coverage. The final test run is still open.

links.scope: Packaged Windows passed four journeys. It recorded 100 presentations, 105 revokes, a real background timer slowdown, and all 32 command outcomes during a held reply. No stale display appeared.
limitations: The test measured retirement when the window became hidden. It checked timer expiry separately in a visible window. The check for those deadlines under background throttling is still open.

links.scope: Chrome showed a saved change from another client. On the next external save, it kept the user's unsaved edit and reported the conflict. The newer saved revision stayed intact.
limitations: This run covered draft conflicts on the local managed server. The combined Chrome and Windows qualification is still open.

links.scope: Chrome showed the new system after the automation client lost the save reply. Retrying the same request returned the original result. The database recorded one change.
limitations: A separate, already connected client retried with the same registered identity on the running server. Server restart has separate evidence.

links.scope: Chrome revoked takeover and switched workspaces while a save was running. The save finished once in the original workspace. When Chrome returned, it showed the saved field and kept the takeover panel closed.
limitations: This test used a system save and two workspaces on the local managed server. Model and conversation jobs have separate coverage.

links.scope: Four packaged Windows journeys passed again. In 105 revokes, the slowest took 11.5 ms. The test matched all 32 queued commands to recorded outcomes and saw no stale presentation.
limitations: Hiding the window retired its lease. The check for deadlines while the window runs in the background is still open.

links.scope: Chrome read an older list reply after showing a newer save. The Manage table kept the newer result and the takeover panel stayed closed.
limitations: This run tested the Manage table. Draft edits and delivery after a workspace change have separate checks.

links.scope: When the test account lost access, Chrome returned control to the user. The server denied saved-state reads, new changes and retries. Restoring access kept the original save and did not restore takeover.
limitations: The test used a synthetic account on the local server. The test did not verify signing in again after access was restored.

links.scope: Chrome tried to save a stale draft from the takeover popup. The unsaved field stayed intact. Manual controls returned when the request ended. The newer saved revision stayed intact, and the browser sent no request to grant takeover.
limitations: This run covered a save conflict. The timeout check for a hidden window remains open.

links.scope: Chrome finished reading a delayed server reply after the user selected Revoke. The browser sent no context, and neither agent request returned context.
limitations: This run checked a held reply. It did not measure the context deadline.

links.scope: Four packaged Windows tests and three Chrome runs passed on the same source. The Chrome runs covered timing, tab isolation, and save behavior. The report records counts, timing, and the exact file hashes.
limitations: Chrome used a local managed server. Both hosts used synthetic data. Background deadlines and final roadmap qualification have separate checks.

links.scope: After an interruption, Chrome received the exact saved change, displayed the new revision, and restored the connection in 1.35 seconds.
limitations: The test used the local managed server and a disposable database.

links.scope: Chrome received a delayed reply after Revoke. The takeover panel stayed closed, and Chrome kept the user's focus and current page.
limitations: The current combined run tested Chrome. The packaged Windows test uses its own run.

links.scope: Rollback disabled all 12 optional routes and returned control to the user. The saved system, open draft, audit history, and record of the original save survived.
limitations: The test covered already-open Chrome pages. Opening a new page during rollback remains unverified.

links.scope: The managed app previewed three proposed changes and returned an identifier for their exact order and inputs. The saved systems stayed unchanged. The app refused a stale saved revision and a different workspace.
limitations: This verifies the preview only. Approval and execution still need implementation and testing.

links.scope: Shared preview checks reject proposed steps that claim approval, add a workspace, reuse a retry key, or use a saved revision after an earlier step changes it.
limitations: The checks cover preview inputs. The app still needs separate checks for approval decisions, changes to authority, and recovery after a lost response.

links.scope: Application tests use simulated app popup and chat callers for whole-plan and per-step approval. They update one exact test record.
limitations: The tests simulate verified callers. App popup and authenticated chat wiring and tests remain open.

links.scope: Actual SQLite preserved one decision from two competing requests and recovered the decision on reopen. A separate in-memory transaction test checked rollback at deadline or caller retirement.
limitations: This proves local storage behavior. Approved step execution and managed server qualification remain open.

links.scope: Separate desktop pairing grants plan review only in the authorized workspace. The grant has no direct editing, conversation or window control permissions.
limitations: The standard app keeps this pairing mode unavailable until the plan approval interface is connected.

links.scope: A pinned desktop connector test staged one plan despite retries. The route denied direct edits and agent-supplied decisions. It withheld results after expiry or retired authority.
limitations: This test used an isolated pinned TLS connector with an in-memory store. Normal Desktop approval and request wiring still need implementation.

links.scope: A local pinned desktop fixture with in-memory storage verifies that new clone proposals use the exact saved source. It refuses missing and stale clone revisions. An authorized exact retry preserves the first proposal after a saved edit.
limitations: The normal desktop approval screen and approved execution remain open.

links.scope: The actual stdio SDK used pinned local HTTPS and an in-memory record to stage and find one exact pending proposal. A separate pinned response test rejected a mismatched step count.
limitations: These tests used local fixtures. Normal app activation and the managed plan-review tools remain open.

links.scope: The exact user approval list survived SQLite reopen. Separate in-memory tests proved scope, expiry, the 32-live-request limit and rollback with the plan record.
limitations: The desktop and browser approval screens still need to use this list through their authenticated app ports.

links.scope: The desktop approval service checks the live requesting client and active workspace through the owned transaction. Local tests hold scope retirement and expiry before commit or before reply.
limitations: The evidence is scoped to the approval service. It does not establish managed browser or authenticated chat behavior.

links.scope: The desktop bridge binds approval to the exact view seen in one window. Tests refuse an old view ID when reopening the same proposal, suppress an ineligible open and retire only the exact dismissed view.
limitations: The bridge fixture checks exact view validation. It does not exercise the managed host or execute a proposed change.

links.scope: Desktop Settings now opens the shared approval dialog. Focused UI and preload tests cover whole-plan and individual approval, exact saved revisions, cancellation, closing with an outstanding reply, and moving to another workspace.
limitations: Focused popup and preload verification do not close native end-to-end or cross-channel qualification.
